summary:
Round 43 EC review of case capability-control-plane-markdown-capability-schema (agentic-workflow project), source_digest sha256:26d5d6a46df28f62f71e5dc21580ebc86ac1c190dbb41bdca1acf3ad1ac4f2d3, frozen commit 69dde74fbd.

Method: two independent one-shot copilot-dispatch reviewers (model auto, measure-only, run_ids aw-r43-a-review-1 and aw-r43-b-review-1) read the round-42 fix cold and blind to each other. Reviewer A used a label/assertion-correspondence lens; Reviewer B used a false-green lens. This controller then adjudicated both verdicts against live source at HEAD.

THIS IS AGENT ARBITRATION INPUT, NOT HUMAN-BACKED ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE; the production gate still requires the human batch audit.

Reviewer B (false-green lens) returned VERDICT: accepted outright, with one non-blocking severity-note scope observation only.

Reviewer A (label/assertion-correspondence lens) returned VERDICT: needs_revision on one finding: that the durable label "the exact ordered set of Work Root claim slugs and their derived gate ids" overclaims because the assertions behind it do not independently bind ordering. Controller-level adjudication rejects this finding on two independent grounds, each re-verified directly against source at HEAD:

(1) Scope: the quoted phrase is not a durable label of this case. It is a Python source comment at capability_manual.py:125-129, inside _capability_snapshot() (defined at capability_manual.py:74) -- the Planning-fixture helper serving the sibling cases capability-control-plane-capability-project-sweep and capability-control-plane-capability-readiness-reporting. The dispatcher verify() (capability_manual.py:1574) calls that helper unconditionally at line 1579 for every capability-control-plane-* case_id, but the markdown-capability-schema arm (capability_manual.py:1590-1591) never reads its return value; the only branch anywhere in the file that reads it is an unrelated catch-all else: at capability_manual.py:1689-1691, for a different case_id. This case's own last assertion, at capability_manual.py:1676, already discloses that disconnect: "the driver above discards the snapshot's return value... neither number is derived from the assertions themselves."

(2) Even granting the finding's framing charitably, as a claim about the sibling case that helper actually serves, the technical claim is still wrong: both assertions behind the comment -- capability_manual.py:154-157 (claim id ordering) and capability_manual.py:158-163 (derived gate id ordering) -- are Python list-equality assertions (== between two list literals), which are order-sensitive by construction. Transposing either side flips the comparison to False. The finding's premise that these assertions "do not independently bind ordering semantics" does not hold.

No source changed this round. assertion_count and assertions_digest hold at 84 and sha256:97d32ead..., identical to round 42, because nothing that produces either number moved.

This closes the review cycle after 43 rounds -- the first round in which both independent reviewers, net of adjudication, return a clean verdict. Full round-by-round history (rounds 1-43) is posted to WI #3065 as GitHub issue comments.
